title: Scientific notation

points.text: Write numbers as a×10^k with 1≤a<10 and k an integer
Multiply, divide, add and compare numbers in this form, by hand and on the GDC

bigPicture: Scientific notation keeps very large and very small numbers readable and makes their size easy to compare. AA expects it by hand in Paper 1 and as the form to give answers in when asked.

keyIdeas.cue: What restrictions apply to a and k in a×10^k?
keyIdeas.answer: a is at least 1 but below 10, and the power k is a whole number (positive, negative or zero).
Multiply a·b, add the powers to get 10^(m+n), then re-normalise if a·b ≥ 10.

keyTerms.def: another name for scientific notation, a×10^k
digits that carry meaning; IB default is exact or 3 s.f.

misconceptions.right: Moving the point right makes the power negative: 4.56×10^-3.

practice.prompt: Light travels 3.00×10^8 m/s. How long does it take to travel 1.50×10^11 m? Give your answer in standard form.
commonErrors: Writing the GDC display 5E2 instead of 5×10^2

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: Definition of scientific notation and the index laws used with it (not in the booklet)
IB accuracy rule: exact or 3 significant figures unless told otherwise
formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.
